title: Erdős Problem #1151: Limit Points of Lagrange Interpolation at Chebyshev Nodes
description: For Lagrange interpolation at Chebyshev nodes, prove that for any closed set A in [-1,1], there exists a continuous function f such that A is the set of limit points of the interpolation values.

meta.author: Erdős (1941), Vértesi (1999)
originalContributions: chebyshevNode: formal definition as cos((2k+1)π/(2n)), proved in [-1,1]
lagrangeInterp: formal Lagrange interpolation operator using Finset.prod/sum

erdos_1151_convergent_case: singleton limit point A={y} as special case

meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: erdos_1941_divergence (Erdős 1941: divergence at rational cosines x=cos(pπ/q)), erdos_1151_conjecture (the open Problem #1151: all closed A ⊆ [-1,1] are realizable as limit point sets).

overview.historicalContext: Lagrange interpolation at Chebyshev nodes is a central topic in approximation theory. The Chebyshev nodes x_k^(n) = cos((2k+1)π/(2n)) are the optimal interpolation nodes: they minimize the maximum error for polynomial interpolation over [-1,1], avoiding the Runge phenomenon that plagues equispaced nodes. Despite their optimality for smooth functions, Faber (1914) proved that no choice of nodes can guarantee uniform convergence for all continuous functions. Erdős (1941) strengthened this by showing that for x = cos(pπ/q) with p, q odd, the Lagrange interpolation values 𝓛ⁿf(x) at Chebyshev nodes can diverge to ∞ for continuous f. In a 1943 paper, Erdős claimed (apparently without full proof) that for any closed A ⊆ [-1,1] and suitable x, there exists continuous f realizing A as the set of limit points. Vértesi (1999) listed this as Problem 2.41 in his problems list on interpolation, and it remains open.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that for any closed A ⊆ [-1,1] and suitable x ∈ [-1,1], there exists continuous f such that A is the set of limit points of 𝓛ⁿf(x).
overview.text: We formalize the problem, defining Chebyshev nodes, Lagrange interpolation, and limit point sets. Chebyshev nodes are the roots of T_n (the n-th Chebyshev polynomial), given by cos((2k+1)π/(2n)) for k=0,...,n-1. The Lagrange interpolation polynomial 𝓛ⁿf(x) = Σₖ f(xₖ) ℓₖ(x) is the unique polynomial of degree ≤ n-1 agreeing with f at all n nodes. The limit point set of a sequence is the set of all its cluster points. We axiomatize Erdős's 1941 result (divergence) and the open conjecture, then derive two special cases.
overview.proofStrategy: Define the mathematical objects and state the conjecture as axioms. Derive special cases (singleton, full interval) from the conjecture. Prove that limit point sets of bounded sequences are topologically closed.
keyInsights: Chebyshev nodes are the roots of T_n: cos((2k+1)π/(2n)), optimal for minimax approximation
Distinctness of nodes proved via Real.strictAntiOn_cos: cosine is strictly decreasing on [0,π]
limitPointSet_isClosed: the complement is open via the reverse triangle inequality — key topological fact
Erdős 1941: at rational cosines x=cos(pπ/q), interpolation can diverge to ∞ for continuous f
The conjecture would give a complete realizability theorem: every closed A ⊆ [-1,1] is achievable
Special cases: convergence (A={y}) and density (A=[-1,1]) both follow immediately from the conjecture
prerequisites: Topology: closed sets, cluster points, lim sup

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #1151 formalized: Chebyshev nodes (proved in [-1,1] and distinct), Lagrange interpolation operator, limit point set (proved closed for bounded sequences). Erdős 1941 divergence result and open conjecture axiomatized. Two special cases proved as corollaries. 3 theorems, 8 definitions, 184 lines, 2 axioms.
conclusion.implications: If proved, the conjecture would give a complete topological classification of the limit behaviors of Lagrange interpolation at Chebyshev nodes: they are exactly the closed subsets of [-1,1]. This would be analogous to classical results on divergence sets of Fourier series. The Chebyshev node framework also connects to potential theory and logarithmic capacity in the complex plane.
openQuestions: Prove the full Erdős conjecture: every closed A ⊆ [-1,1] is realizable as a limit point set
Characterize exactly which x ∈ [-1,1] are 'suitable' — does the conjecture hold for all x?
Use Baire category methods to prove existence of f (generic function approach)
Extend to other node sequences: is the result true for Gauss-Legendre or Gauss-Lobatto nodes?

crossReferences.description: Both involve approximation of continuous functions on [-1,1]; bisection and Chebyshev interpolation are two approaches to root-finding and function approximation
Both are axiomatized Erdős-era results about asymptotic/limit behavior of sequences
